A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same SegMoTE study, with corresponding equations, seven figures and four tables. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original SegMoTE segmentation results, decoder fine-tuning experiments and expert/prompt-token ablations.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original segmentation experiments and ablation outcomes, including Tables 1–4 and Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: The expert tokens, MoTE routing, Progressive Prompt Tokenization and segmentation/load-balancing objectives are unchanged. The decoder fine-tuning variant in Section 4.2 already appears in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MedSeg-HQ dataset composition and segmentation tasks, with the same out-of-domain evaluations on ISLES, SegThor and TotalSegmentator MRI. Modality coverage and ablation scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Figure 5 and Table 1 retain SAM, SAM 2, MedSAM, Huang et al., SAM-Med2D and IMIS. Table 2 retains its existing subset of SAM, SAM2, SAM-Med2D and IMIS; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains 512×512 inputs, the patient-independent 9:1 split, Dice evaluation, SAM-Base, and the same point/box prompting and decoder fine-tuning settings. Training settings and ablation configurations are unchanged.

E4.justification: The expert-selection statistics and expert-count experiments in Figure 6, routing visualizations in Figure 7, and query-count/without-PPT ablations in Table 4 are identical. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The expert-selection frequency reporting in Figure 6 is unchanged.

E6.justification: All four tables retain identical entries, and all seven figure images match. For example, Table 1 reports ISLES Dice scores of 77.30 for SegMoTE and 71.24 for IMIS in both versions; the accompanying findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 retain the same routing, noisy gating, expert-load and loss definitions. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about SAM capability preservation, modality adaptation, automatic prompting and performance using 17M trainable parameters and approximately 0.15M masks.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of dataset quality, expert specialization and routing. Section 3.4 preserves the limitation concerning multiclass interference, and the conclusion retains future exploration of 3D and medical video data.

D1.justification: V2 adds an InMyDreammer/SegMoTE GitHub repository link beneath the author block, absent from v1. This supplies new access information; implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and data-curation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 54 references and related-work arguments are retained. Changed bibliography page pointers reflect pagination changes, without adding cited works or revising research positioning.

P1.justification: The title block gains a repository line and the arXiv version/date header changes. The prose, terminology, section sequence and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Layout reflow moves Figure 1 from page 1 to 2, Figure 5 from page 6 to 7, and Table 2 from page 7 to 8. Figure artwork, table structures and captions are unchanged; other shifts concern spacing and page breaks.

improvement.justification: The new first-page repository link provides a modest improvement in implementation-resource discoverability over v1. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged, with no substantive loss from the layout reflow. This benefit concerns access information; the PDFs alone do not establish repository availability or completeness.
